title: Prisma Studio Introduction
description: Explore, manage, and debug your application data visually using Prisma Studio's zero-config web interface.

data.text: **Prisma Studio** is a visual, browser-based database management interface integrated directly into the Prisma CLI. It allows developers to inspect models, view and edit rows, traverse complex relational links, and filter datasets without installing standalone GUI tools or writing ad-hoc SQL queries.

data.title: Starting Studio via Terminal
data.content: Run this command in your project root where schema.prisma is located.
data.code:
# Launch Studio on default port 5555
npx prisma studio

# Launch on a custom port or specific host
npx prisma studio --port 5556 --browser none

data.text: When launched, Prisma Studio reads your compiled schema metadata (DMMF) and starts a local web server (typically at `http://localhost:5555`). It automatically reflects all models, fields, enums, and foreign key relations.

data.title: Core Features
items: **Visual Relation Traversal**: Click directly on a foreign key or relation field to open the linked record in a drawer without losing your context.
**Interactive CRUD**: Double-click table cells to edit values directly, insert new records, or select multiple rows to delete them in batch.
**Staged Changes**: Edits are highlighted and staged in the browser interface; changes are only committed to the database when you click 'Save changes'.
**Dynamic Filtering & Sorting**: Filter records by multiple compound conditions (e.g. `createdAt > 2024-01-01` AND `role = ADMIN`) with intuitive dropdowns.
**JSON & Array Support**: Native JSON viewer and editor for PostgreSQL `JSONB` fields.

data.title: Team Collaboration Tip
data.text: Prisma Studio is safe for local development, but avoid exposing it on public production servers without authentication. For remote team collaboration, use managed cloud consoles like Neon Console, Supabase Studio, or Prisma Data Platform.

data.title: Hands-on: Test Data Seeding via Studio
data.description: Use Prisma Studio to verify that your seed data was created properly and test foreign key constraints.
steps: Navigate to the `User` tab and create a new row with a unique email.
Navigate to the `Post` tab and create a post linked to the user you just created.
Observe how the relation picker dropdown allows selecting the author seamlessly.
Click 'Save 2 changes' to commit the records.
data.expectedOutcome: Both records are persisted to PostgreSQL with valid relational integrity.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `npx prisma studio` provides an instant visual interface for your database.
Staged changes prevent accidental data mutation.
Great for rapid manual testing, debugging edge cases, and inspecting JSONB columns.
